messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a regression on nightly for continuous batching with long-context streams. P95 latency up ~20% on a03-GPU hosts.
jon: ugh, same cluster here. Any correlation with recent kernel selection changes?
sasha: I rolled kernel-selector rev 3.4.2 yesterday (better int8 gemm path). Could be falling back in weird cases.
andy: quick dump from the failing run: `nvidia-smi` shows GPU mem used steady but host RAM spikes then OOM-kv-eviction. Snippet: `KV cache headroom: 0.12, watermark=0.75 -> triggered eviction`
elena: profiling (small sample):
```
Perf summary:
- avg token latency: 86ms -> 105ms
- p95: 210ms -> 255ms
- kernel fallback count: 42
- kv-eviction events: 18
```
maria: Looks like batch formation admitted larger batches without considering KV headroom; when eviction fires, kernel switches and we incur copy+recompile cost.
jon: Agreed. Continuous batcher only used `max_batch_tokens` + `queue_time_ms` today. No kv-aware gating.
sasha: The new kernel path regresses when the model's past length > 1600 because compilation picks the fused attention kernel which doesn't play nicely with partial KV evictions.
andy: Repro command I used: `./run_infer --model llama-2-13b --seq 4096 --stream=1 --batch_budget=2000` -> reproduces p95 jump.
elena: Telemetry shows spike in `kernel_recompile_ms` around the same time as `kv_eviction_start`.
maria: Proposal: change admission policy to check `kv_free_tokens >= batch_token_estimate + eviction_margin`. eviction_margin = 256 initially. If not enough, reduce per-request token allowance or force smaller kernel variant.
sasha: Also add a soft headroom watermark (0.25) to the batch shaper: if headroom below watermark, prefer non-fused kernel that tolerates eviction (slower per-token but avoids recompile).
jon: Another idea: conservative token budgeting for continuous streams from same connection. If they've been streaming > 1k tokens in last minute, bias them to small batches.
andy: I can prototype admission change. I'll add a flag `--kv-aware-admit` and a metric `kv_admit_rejects`.
elena: For the short term, can we rollback kernel-selector 3.4.2 on a subset and A/B? We need to prove causality.
sasha: Yes — I'll schedule canary rollback on a03 pool for 30m after lunch.
maria: Action list: 1) andy: PR for `kv-aware-admit` + tests (unit + small e2e) 2) sasha: canary rollback 3) elena: add telemetry hooks for `kernel_recompile_ms` and `kv_eviction_reason` 4) jon: add a quick gating rule in batch shaper to check `kv_headroom` before admission.
jon: I'll also add an integration test case that simulates partial KV eviction during batch assembly.
andy: Initial PR draft in my branch `andy/kv-admit-heuristic`. ping me for review.
elena: FYI perf-bot just posted an alert: `nightly-build-2310001100` failed p95 threshold. :warning:
perf-bot: @eng-runtime flagged p95 latency increase +22% on nightly, link: https://perf.internal/runs/2310001100
maria: Good. Let's meet 30m to sync after the canary starts.
sasha: thanks all, will update in thread when canary rolls. :thumbsup:
